title: Erebuni founded
description: King Argishti I of Urartu builds a fortress on a hill that later becomes Yerevan, as recorded on its foundation stone.

title: Artaxata founded
description: King Artaxias I, founder of an independent Armenian dynasty, builds a new capital on the Araxes.

title: Battle of Tigranocerta
place: Tigranocerta (site disputed, shown near Silvan), Turkey
description: A Roman army under Lucullus defeats Tigranes the Great, whose empire had reached from the Caspian to the Mediterranean.

title: Tiridates I crowned by Nero
description: The Parthian prince receives the Armenian crown from the Roman emperor, the compromise that founds the Arsacid dynasty of Armenia.

title: Armenia adopts Christianity
description: King Tiridates III is baptised by Gregory the Illuminator and makes Christianity the religion of the kingdom, by tradition the first state to do so.

title: Armenia divided between Rome and Persia
description: The two empires partition the kingdom, with about four fifths going to the Sasanians.

title: Armenian alphabet
description: The monk Mesrop Mashtots devises an alphabet for Armenian, which is first used to translate the Bible.

title: Battle of Avarayr
description: Armenians under Vardan Mamikonian fight a Sasanian army that had come to enforce Zoroastrianism, and though they lose they later keep the right to remain Christian.

title: Ashot I crowned king
description: The caliph and the Byzantine emperor both recognise the Bagratid prince as king, restoring an Armenian kingdom after more than four centuries.

title: Ani becomes the capital
description: King Ashot III moves his court to Ani, which grows into a city famous for its walls and churches.

title: Seljuks take Ani
description: Sultan Alp Arslan captures the city after a siege of twenty-five days and kills or enslaves much of its population.

title: Leo I crowned king of Cilicia
description: The Armenian prince of Cilicia is crowned with the backing of the pope and the Holy Roman Emperor, founding a kingdom on the Mediterranean allied with the Crusaders.

title: Fall of Sis
description: The Mamluks capture the capital and its king, ending the last Armenian kingdom.

title: Catholicosate returns to Etchmiadzin
description: A church council moves the seat of the head of the Armenian Church from Sis in Cilicia back to its first home.

title: First Armenian printed book
description: Hakob Meghapart prints the Urbatagirk, the beginning of Armenian printing.

title: Shah Abbas deports the Armenians
description: Retreating before the Ottomans, the shah moves several hundred thousand people from the Ararat plain and Julfa into Iran, where the merchants of Julfa found New Julfa at Isfahan.

title: Battle of Halidzor
description: The Armenians of Syunik under David Bek defeat an Ottoman army, the high point of a short-lived self-governing principality.

title: Russians capture Yerevan
description: The army of Ivan Paskevich takes the fortress of Erivan, and eastern Armenia passes from Persian to Russian rule.

title: Sasun and the Hamidian massacres
description: The suppression of an Armenian revolt in Sasun begins two years of massacres across the Ottoman Empire in which at least 100,000 Armenians are killed.

title: Battle of Sardarabad
description: Armenian troops and volunteers halt the Ottoman advance on Yerevan in a battle of nine days.

title: First Republic declared
description: After the breakup of the Transcaucasian federation the Armenian National Council declares independence, creating the first Armenian state since the Middle Ages.

title: Soviet rule established
description: Defeated in a war with Turkey, the government hands power to the Bolsheviks and signs away its western lands in the Treaty of Alexandropol.

title: Treaty of Kars
description: The Soviet republics of the Caucasus and Turkey fix the border that still stands, leaving Kars and Mount Ararat in Turkey.

title: Yerevan demonstrations
description: On the fiftieth anniversary of the deportations of 1915 a large crowd demands recognition of the Armenian genocide, and a memorial is built at Tsitsernakaberd two years later.

title: Karabakh movement begins
description: Hundreds of thousands rally in support of the request of the Nagorno-Karabakh regional council to be transferred from Soviet Azerbaijan to Soviet Armenia.

title: Spitak earthquake
description: An earthquake destroys Spitak and much of Leninakan and kills at least 25,000 people.

title: Vote for independence
description: Voters approve leaving the Soviet Union almost unanimously, and independence is declared two days later.

title: Shooting in parliament
description: Gunmen kill the prime minister, the speaker and six others in the National Assembly.

title: Post-election protests broken up
description: Ten people die when police and troops disperse protests against the result of the presidential election.

title: Velvet Revolution
description: Serzh Sargsyan resigns as prime minister after weeks of peaceful protests, and their leader Nikol Pashinyan takes office in May.
